title: improv·artist · minimal (Lee Ufan)
mutation_directive: improv artist: minimal via Lee Ufan

improv_extras.practice: single brushstroke per canvas; mono-ha; stone and steel as encounter

v1.feedback: Excellent restraint and conceptual clarity — the single brushstroke emerging via phased particle animation genuinely captures Lee Ufan's economy of gesture. The mono-ha 'encounter' feels present in how particles occupy negative space deliberately, though the stroke could benefit from subtle texture variation (slight z-depth jitter or ink-bleed edge softening) to escape feeling digitally perfect. The muted palette and density gradient from stroke center are spot-on; consider adding very subtle opacity modulation based on distance-from-gesture-start to enhance the 'hand leaving paper' quality that defines his work.

v2.feedback: Excellent translation of Lee Ufan's single-gesture philosophy into particle form — the phased reveal with pressure variation, ink-bleed at edges, and lifting at stroke end all show genuine conceptual engagement. The restrained charcoal palette on warm paper and the subtle paper-texture jitter demonstrate restraint. Minor issue: the form occupies center-frame well but could benefit from slightly bolder stroke width range (currently 2.0-3.5) to better match the confidence of Ufan's physical marks, and the taper could be more aggressive (currently 30% reduction) to emphasize the lifted brush.
